rubric.description: Uses the correct conversion relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing °C = K − 273 or an equivalent relation.

rubric.why: Subtracting 273 from 300 K gives 27°C.
rubric.description: Gives the converted temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct answer, 27°C.

items.followUp: Derive the second equation of motion, s = ut + ½at², using a speed-time graph.

rubric.why: The displacement is the area under the speed-time graph, which is a trapezium.
rubric.description: Expresses displacement as the area under the graph.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for s = ½(u + v)t or an equivalent expression.

rubric.why: The first equation of motion relates the change in velocity to acceleration and time.
rubric.description: Relates time to velocity and acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct rearrangement of v = u + at.

rubric.why: Substituting the expression for time into the area equation leads to the required relation.
rubric.description: Substitutes for time and simplifies.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct substitution or the resulting identity 2as = (u + v)(v − u).

rubric.why: Expanding and rearranging gives the third equation of motion.
rubric.description: States the third equation of motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for v² = u² + 2as or an equivalent rearrangement.

modelAnswer: Displacement is the area under the speed-time graph, which is a trapezium: s = ½(u + v)t.
From the first equation of motion, v = u + at, so t = (v − u)/a.
Substitute for t: s = ½(u + v)(v − u)/a.

items.followUp: Define potential energy and derive the expression for the potential energy of a body raised through height h.

rubric.why: Potential energy is associated with a body's position or configuration.
rubric.description: Defines potential energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining it as energy possessed due to position or configuration.

rubric.why: A suitable example shows energy stored due to position.
rubric.description: Gives an example of potential energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant example, such as a raised body.

rubric.why: The force that must be overcome in raising the body is its weight, mg.
rubric.description: Identifies the force involved in raising the body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the body's weight is mg.

rubric.why: Work done against gravity in raising the body is stored as potential energy.
rubric.description: Derives the potential-energy formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using work = force × distance and obtaining PE = mgh.

modelAnswer: Potential energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its position or configuration.
For example, a body raised above the ground has potential energy.
To raise a body of mass m through height h, work is done against its weight: F = mg.
This work is stored as potential energy; therefore, PE = mgh.

items.followUp: A perpendicular force of 80 N acts on a spanner 0.25 m from a nut. Calculate the torque.

rubric.why: The force and perpendicular distance are needed, with the distance expressed in SI units.
rubric.description: Records the given data and converts the distance to metres.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying F = 100 N and r = 0.10 m.

rubric.why: Torque equals force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the pivot.
rubric.description: Writes the torque formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for torque = force × perpendicular distance.

rubric.why: Substitution of the given SI values into the formula is required.
rubric.description: Substitutes the values into the formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct substitution.

rubric.why: Multiplying 100 by 0.10 gives a torque magnitude of 10.
rubric.description: Calculates the numerical value.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining 10.

rubric.why: Torque is measured in newton-metres.
rubric.description: Gives the answer with the correct unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 10 N m.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 100 N; r = 10 cm = 0.10 m
Therefore, the torque is 10 N m.

items.followUp: A steel wire 2 m long with cross-sectional area 4 × 10⁻⁵ m² extends by 2 mm under a force of 8,000 N. Calculate its Young's modulus.

rubric.why: The given quantities and extension in metres are needed for the calculation.
rubric.description: Records the data and converts the extension to SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for recording the given values and converting 1 mm to 1 × 10⁻³ m.

rubric.why: Young's modulus is defined as stress divided by strain.
rubric.description: Writes the Young's modulus relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Y = stress/strain or its equivalent.

rubric.why: Using stress = F/A and strain = ΔL/L gives the working formula.
rubric.description: Rearranges the relation into a formula using the given quantities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Y = FL/(AΔL).

rubric.why: The SI values give a modulus of 2 × 10¹¹ Pa.
rubric.description: Substitutes the SI values and calculates the result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution and obtaining 2 × 10¹¹.

rubric.why: The SI unit of Young's modulus is pascal.
rubric.description: States the final answer with its unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 2 × 10¹¹ Pa.

modelAnswer: Given: L = 1 m; A = 5 × 10⁻⁵ m²; F = 10,000 N; ΔL = 1 mm = 1 × 10⁻³ m
Substitution: Y = (10,000 N × 1 m) ÷ (5 × 10⁻⁵ m² × 1 × 10⁻³ m)
